root_cause.text: The Tegra crypto driver registered inherently asynchronous AES/AEAD/hash/CMAC algorithms without the CRYPTO_ALG_ASYNC flag in their cra_flags, so the crypto API misclassified them as synchronous and selected them for synchronous-only users.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE/commit explicitly says the driver “failed to set the CRYPTO_ALG_ASYNC on its asynchronous algorithms, causing the crypto API to select them for users that request only synchronous algorithms,” and the patch adds CRYPTO_ALG_ASYNC across tegra-se-aes.c and tegra-se-hash.c while removing ignored CRYPTO_ALG_TYPE_* flags.

This CMAC registration uses only CRYPTO_ALG_TYPE_AHASH and fails to include CRYPTO_ALG_ASYNC even though the implementation is request-driven and asynchronous, matching the stated root cause.
This HMAC hash registration still omits CRYPTO_ALG_ASYNC while advertising fallback support, so the inherently asynchronous implementation is likewise misregistered as synchronous.

bic_trace_step.reason:
The snippet is sufficient because it contains both the request handling logic showing these algorithms are engine-backed/asynchronous and the algorithm registration tables with the cra_flags values. The root cause is missing CRYPTO_ALG_ASYNC on inherently asynchronous registrations. This file clearly uses the crypto engine async path: skcipher requests are queued with "crypto_transfer_skcipher_request_to_engine(ctx->se->engine, req)", AEAD requests with "crypto_transfer_aead_request_to_engine(ctx->se->engine, req)", and CMAC/ahash requests with "crypto_transfer_hash_request_to_engine(ctx->se->engine, req)", then completed later via "crypto_finalize_*_request(...)" in the do_one_req callbacks. So these are inherently asynchronous implementations.

For skcipher, most entries are correctly flagged async, e.g. CBC/ECB/CTR have ".cra_flags = CRYPTO_ALG_TYPE_SKCIPHER | CRYPTO_ALG_ASYNC". However, the XTS skcipher entry lacks any cra_flags line entirely in its base initializer, despite also using the same async engine path via tegra_aes_do_one_req and crypto_transfer_skcipher_request_to_engine(). That means the vulnerable construct is present for XTS.

For AEAD, both registrations are missing CRYPTO_ALG_ASYNC: the "gcm(aes)" and "ccm(aes)" entries have base fields such as ".cra_name", ".cra_driver_name", ".cra_priority", ".cra_blocksize", etc., but no ".cra_flags = ... | CRYPTO_ALG_ASYNC" at all, even though they are processed asynchronously through tegra_gcm_do_one_req / tegra_ccm_do_one_req and queued with crypto_transfer_aead_request_to_engine().

For CMAC/ahash, the registration explicitly sets ".cra_flags = CRYPTO_ALG_TYPE_AHASH" without CRYPTO_ALG_ASYNC, while requests are queued asynchronously with crypto_transfer_hash_request_to_engine() and finalized later in tegra_cmac_do_one_req. This exactly matches the root cause.

Therefore the vulnerable construct is present, and the fix is not yet present because the async-backed XTS/AEAD/CMAC registrations do not advertise CRYPTO_ALG_ASYNC.
